_note: Settings for exporting the player's mission as a real NASA GMAT script. GMAT (General Mission Analysis Tool) is NASA's open-source mission design program, built at Goddard and used on real flight projects. A script written in this format opens in GMAT and propagates. That is the point of the feature: the mission a 12-year-old designed in the game can be loaded into the same tool a NASA analyst uses.
_syntaxNote: GMAT's own GUI writes scripts in exactly this shape: 'Create <Type> <name>;' for resources, then 'GMAT <name>.<Property> = <value>;' for each setting, '%' to start a comment, and a single 'BeginMissionSequence;' after every resource is created and before the first command. Resource names ChemicalTank and ChemicalThruster are the R2018a-and-later spellings (they were FuelTank and Thruster before that).
_propagatorNote: A Prince-Dormand 78 integrator, which is GMAT's workhorse for interplanetary propagation, with the accuracy GMAT itself defaults to.
_coefficientNote: Drag and reflectivity coefficients. 2.2 and 1.8 are GMAT's own defaults and the usual first-cut values for a boxy spacecraft.
_bodyNote: Which GMAT central body and coordinate system each mission uses, and the point masses worth including in the force model. Keyed by scenario id. GMAT calls the Moon 'Luna'.
_outputNote: What GMAT should draw and write when the script runs, so the file does something visible the moment it is opened rather than propagating silently.
